page: OVHcloud b2-15 is a general-purpose virtual server hosted on a KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Haswell processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs with 4 physical cores and no hyperthreading, providing a direct one-to-one mapping of virtual to physical resources. The system is equipped with 15.0 GB of RAM, which translates to 3.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 100 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates that the b2-15 delivers modest compute performance. Its single-core stress-ng CPU performance of 959.69 is positioned in the bottom 10 percent, while its multi-core score of 3669.99 falls in the bottom 25 percent. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read operations achieve an average bandwidth of 347.69 GB/sec, but uncached large-block reads and writes drop to a weaker 37.17 GB/sec and 22.32 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET performance are more competitive, with Redis handling 5.93 million operations per second, placing it in the middle 50 percent of tested servers.

The primary tradeoff of the b2-15 is its reliance on older Intel Haswell architecture, which lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX. This limitation is reflected in its poor performance during medium-sized LLM inference tasks, where it achieves only 5.77 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B model. However, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures stable, non-burstable performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a balanced resource density for workloads that do not require high-performance compute. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, basic database operations, lightweight Redis caching, and standard web serving.
